question.leadin: This policy was reinforced by the Bantu Education Act.
question.text: Name this policy, which Stephen Biko protested in South Africa. It called for the racial segregation of blacks and whites.
question.clue: The "I Am Prepared to Die" speech at the Rivonia Trial denounced this system.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Nelson Mandela's trial and imprisonment.
swap.text: At the Rivonia trial, Mandela and other members of this party were tried. The Church street bombings were carried out by this party's uMkhonto we Sizwe, or Spear of the Nation, wing.
swap.clue: After the Sharpeville Massacre, this party formed the militant Spear of the Nation, some of whose members were convicted in the Rivonia Trial.

question.text: This river passes through the cities of Bamako and Timbuktu as well as the capital of its namesake country, Niamey. It enters the Gulf of Guinea.
question.clue: In the 1990s, the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People, or MOSOP, was founded by Ken Saro-Wiwa to protest the exploitation of the oil resources of this river's delta.

swap.text: This African nation, which also suffers from hyperinflation, is led by Robert Mugabe. To "counter" inflation, this nation removed 10 zeros from its currency in 2008, making 10 billion dollars equal to one.
swap.clue: In 1987, Joseph Nkomo, an opposition leader from this country, was coerced into leaving politics after thousands of his supporters were killed in this country's Matabeleland region.

question.leadin: This country's namesake empire fought a protracted war with the Adal Sultanate in the mid-16th century.
question.text: Name this country in the Horn of Africa where that Christian empire was ruled for 700 years by the Solomonic dynasty. This country's final ruler, Haile Selassie, ruled from its capital of Addis Ababa until 1974.
question.answerHtml: Ethiopia [accept Abyssinia or the Ethiopian Empire or the Abyssinian Empire]
question.clue: The Kebra Nagast details the ancient heritage of this country's kings, which it claims descended from the Queen of Sheba and King Solomon.

swap.leadin: One city in this empire included a massive library of Islamic learning at the University of Sankore ["sahn-CORE-eh"].
swap.text: Name this empire, the home of many griots that recorded oral history. One griot epic tells the story of Sundiata Keita founding this empire by beating Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.
swap.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

question.text: The Derg fought a war over the Ogaden ("OH-gah-den") region with this country, at the time led by Siad Barre ("see-AHD BAR-reh"). In 1993, the US launched Operation Gothic Serpent to capture Mohamed Farrah Aidid ("eye-DEED") in this country.
question.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

swap.text: Mugabe served as Prime Minister and President of this country, where he commissioned the Heroes' Acre to be built in Harare.
swap.clue: This country's first president was Canaan Banana, who was arrested in 1997 on charges of sodomy.

question.text: This figure defeated the Sosso king Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina, to found a major African kingdom.
question.clue: She gave birth to a sickly child, a child whose entire family, including his eleven brothers, was killed by an invading Kaniaga ruler, though Sumanguru left this child alive because he thought this boy would die soon enough.

swap.text: Rhodes envisioned a railroad from "Cape to [this city]", allowing British holdings to span the whole African continent. Anwar Sadat and Gamal Abdel Nasser were secular rulers here.
swap.clue: That predecessor city, Fustat, had been burnt by the vizier Shawar.

question.leadin: European imperialism in Africa faced resistance from many local powers, such as the Zulu Kingdom.
question.text: Name this leader of the Zulu during the Zulu War. This ruler consolidated rival tribes to grow Zulu borders and also introduced the "bull horn" army formation.
question.clue: This rival of Zwide has been credited with introducing widespread use of a short stabbing spear called the iklwa, which was an improvement on the assegai.

swap.leadin: This city rests near the junction of the Sobat and White Nile Rivers, and was a plausible site for Victor Prompt's plan to dam the Nile and dry up Egypt.
swap.text: Name this site where two expeditions met in 1898; one from Brazzaville, which got there first, and one under Horatio Kitchener after his victory at Omdurman.
swap.clue: It is probably best known as the location of an 1898 war scare that brought to a head the territorial dispute in Africa between France and Britain, its namesake "incident".

question.leadin: The Lemon project at the College of William & Mary features the donning of stoles made of this cloth for African-American students.
question.text: Name these handwoven textiles which are colorful patterns of interwoven strips of typically silk and cotton that originate from Ghana.
question.clue: The Akan and Ashanti people are associated with this traditional style of cloth. Nancy Pelosi drew ridicule for wearing this fabric at a Black Lives Matter event in 2020.

swap.text: Other Nigerian military leaders during the war included this general, who later took over Nigeria in a 1976 coup, although he transitioned the country back to democracy. He was so popular that he was also Nigeria's democratically elected president from 1999 to 2007.

question.leadin: While fighting this state, Mark Bell won the Victoria Cross for "heroically" slave-driving a group of native sappers into continuing to dig ditches while under heavy fire.
question.text: Identify this kingdom defeated at the battles of Ordashu and Amoaful by Garnett Wolsey in the third of a series of conflicts with the British. It was founded by Osei Tutu.
question.clue: Osei Tutu founded this kingdom, a subgroup of the Akan ethnicity which developed kente cloth.

swap.leadin: Jan Cornelisz Vermeyen's tapestries depict women serving as battlefield nurses during the 1535 conquest of this city, challenging stereotypes that its women were confined to harems.
swap.text: Name this city that changed hands between the Ottomans and the Spanish, acting on behalf of the Hafsid dynasty, throughout the 16th century. This present-day capital city eclipsed nearby Kairouan ("kye-ruh-WAHN") and Mahdia in the 12th century.
swap.clue: Saint Louis died of dysentery while on a crusade to this city This city was established near the site of Mahdia, and it was ruled for centuries by its Hafsid Dynasty.

question.leadin: The Kennedy government turned down his request for aid, instead backing the rival FNLA led by Holden Roberto for its anti-Communist leanings.
question.text: Name this politician, who ascended to power in the wake of the Carnation revolution to become the first president of his nation but died during cancer treatment in Moscow four years later.

swap.text: The United States led from behind in this operation to support the Libyan rebels in 2011. The United States would end this mission after 13 days and hand control over to NATO.

question.leadin: Its first ruler legendarily came down from the sky and married Nneamaku and was named Eri, and its kings employed members of the Ikenga cult as officials.
question.text: Identify this oldest kingdom in Nigeria, which was ruled by secluded kings known as Eze. The British forced its final ruler, Obalike, to leave the kingdom under threat of genocide.

swap.leadin: British troops in this country managed to gain the allegiance of the West Side Boys, an armed militia who dressed as American gang members in the style of Tupac.
swap.text: Name this country where the Revolutionary United Front, led by Foday Sankoh, fought the government in a civil war from 1991 to 2002. The Abidjan Peace Accords created a brief ceasefire in this country's civil war that only ended due to British intervention.
swap.clue: Resentment of this country's Krio elite was exploited by Foday Sankoh, the leader of the Revolutionary United Front, whose use of cocaine-addicted child soldiers is attested in Ishmael Beah's A Long Way Gone.
